clue.text: Arsenal Gooner half-heartedly teased Chelsea toff

definitions.note: a well-to-do young person from the smart Chelsea and Kensington area of London

indicators.note: teased in the sense of combed out or pulled apart, so the letters are worked into a new order
the heart of the fan's word is a pair of Os, and losing half that heart drops one of them

explanation.surface: An Arsenal fan mocks a posh Chelsea supporter, a picture of London football rivalry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' turns GOONER into GONER by losing one of its central Os; 'teased' then shuffles ARSENAL plus GONER. A Gooner is an Arsenal fan, which makes the football reading persuasive.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a 1980s stereotype of the upper-class young set around Sloane Square in Chelsea, a toff by definition.

clue.text: One whose death was staged in rep?

definitions.text: One whose death was staged in rep?

parts.words: One whose death was staged in rep?
parts.note: points to Arthur Miller's play Death of a ..., about Willy Loman, a travelling rep, whose death is put on stage; rep is both repertory theatre and a sales representative

explanation.surface: A question about an actor whose demise was performed in repertory theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rep' reads as repertory theatre but also means a sales representative, and Arthur Miller's play about one is often revived.
explanation.definitionFit: Willy Loman, the hero of Miller's play, is a travelling commercial representative whose death the drama leads to.

clue.text: Reagan vote took time to build, as expected

indicators.note: building something from parts means assembling the remaining letters in a fresh order
took in the sense of took away, so a letter is removed from the phrase

explanation.surface: A political story: a Reagan vote took a while to gather, which was predictable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took' removes T (time) from REAGAN VOTE, and 'to build' rearranges the nine letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens on the whole, typically, is what one would normally expect.

clue.text: Lad's thrown up hotel food

indicators.note: in a down clue thrown up means the word for the lad is written bottom to top

parts.note: a lad is a son
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A boy has vomited his hotel meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown up' works in a down clue as reading upwards; the 's is just 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A British informal word for grub, anything to eat.

clue.text: That's funny, taking Owen back on board; fellow's hardly a team player!

indicators.note: taking means the laugh's letters take the reversed name inside them

parts.note: LOL, laugh out loud, is the texting reaction to something funny

indicators.note: back means the name of Owen is written from right to left

parts.note: the name taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone laughs as Owen is brought into a firm, though the fellow is no collaborator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the name and 'taking' puts it inside the laugh; 'on board' only reinforces the idea of taking someone in.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a person who prefers to act independently rather than cooperate with a group.

clue.text: Part of a cluster used in decoration

definitions.text: Part of a cluster used in decoration

parts.words: Part of a cluster used in decoration
parts.note: the US military award device called an ... cluster is added to a medal ribbon to mark a further award

explanation.surface: Something that forms one element of a bunch used for ornament, like flowers or grapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decoration' suggests ornament, but here it is a military medal; the cluster is the American bronze device of foliage pinned to a ribbon.
explanation.definitionFit: The US award device shows a sprig of tree foliage, so one such leaf is literally part of the cluster.

clue.text: Able to get rubbed out any time, Italian island detectives are in revolution

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: turned round in a revolution, so the island and the detectives are read in reverse order

parts.note: Elba is the Italian island where Napoleon was exiled
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Italian island detectives rising up could be wiped out at any moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in revolution' reverses island and detectives together, giving DICABLE. Elba was Napoleon's place of exile.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be wiped out entirely is capable of being eliminated or removed.

clue.text: Regular intake of booze own men described as potentially toxic

definitions.note: an adjective phrase defining a noun: the gas is described as harmful when breathed in at ground level

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every second letter from the three words

explanation.surface: Men's habitual drinking of their own booze is said to be potentially harmful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regular intake of' takes the even letters of BOOZE OWN MEN; 'described as' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This form of oxygen is a pollutant at ground level and can damage the lungs, so it is a hazardous gas.

clue.text: Boris Johnson's department title repelled warring opponent

parts.note: Johnson was Foreign Secretary, head of the FO, the Foreign Office

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the word for a title is read in reverse

parts.note: a title is a name

explanation.surface: A political story about a department heading rebuffed by a hostile adversary.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Johnson was Foreign Secretary from 2016 to 2018; 'repelled' signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for an enemy in battle, an adversary in war.

clue.text: See 24
Applying Koran, lash usurer

indicators.note: applying in the sense of putting the letters to a new use, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Applying the Koran's punishment of flogging to a moneylender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Applying' signals a rearrangement of KORAN LASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A predatory moneylender charging exorbitant interest is a usurer.

clue.text: Bitter, working in solitary

indicators.note: in places the word for working inside the beer

parts.note: bitter is a kind of ale
ON means working, as in a machine that is on

explanation.surface: Someone sour and busy in isolation, or a beer drinker on their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bitter' reads as an adjective but is the British beer ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being solitary means being by oneself, without company.

clue.text: In America, plenty swing

definitions.meaning: a US informal noun for a large quantity, as in a whole lot
to turn or swerve round, as a vehicle skids sideways

explanation.surface: A note on American swing music being abundant.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a great many in American usage and also to turn sharply or pivot.

clue.text: Machine designed to attract uninhibited women for private entertainment

indicators.note: to attract means to draw in, so the trimmed women go inside the rearranged letters
designed means put together to a new plan, so the letters of the device are rearranged
uninhibited read as without the restraining outer letters, leaving only the middle of the word

explanation.surface: A gadget built to lure free-spirited women for some private fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uninhibited' sheds the outer letters W and N; 'designed' rearranges the device into HCINEMA, and 'to attract' draws the trimmed women into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic setup of big screen and sound system lets you watch films privately at home.

clue.text: Pal scooted round to help with delivery

indicators.note: round means the letters go around and come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A friend zipped about to assist with a delivery, perhaps of a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' rearranges PAL SCOOTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Postcodes are the letter-number strings that let mail be sorted and brought to the right address.

clue.text: A poison coating Lake Ontario's premier shellfish

indicators.note: coating means the poison's letters cover the lake and the initial on both sides

parts.note: bane is an old word for poison, as in henbane
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

indicators.note: premier means first, so only the opening letter of Ontario is used

explanation.surface: A toxic film covering Lake Ontario's finest seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coating' puts L + O (first of Ontario) inside BANE, after A. 'premier' looks like a political title but just means first.
explanation.definitionFit: An edible sea snail with an iridescent shell, also known as ormer, is a mollusc counted as shellfish.

clue.text: Absolutely lovely empty apartment at the front

indicators.note: at the front places the word for the apartment before the other piece

parts.note: a flat is a British word for an apartment

indicators.note: empty means the word is emptied of its contents, leaving just the outside letters

explanation.surface: Praise for a lovely vacant flat facing the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' reduces LOVELY to LY.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny something outright is to deny it completely, in a firm, unqualified way.

clue.text: Unfinished underwear no good for hanging around

indicators.note: unfinished means the word for underwear lacks its final letter

parts.note: lingerie is women's underwear

explanation.surface: Incomplete, worthless underwear left dangling about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' removes the final letter, the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging around means staying on or loitering, waiting before leaving.

clue.text: Curry containers left in the German tube

indicators.note: the containers of a word are its outer letters, which hold the rest

parts.note: der is the German masculine word for the

explanation.surface: Pots of curry left inside some German's pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containers' takes C and Y, the outside letters of CURRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A hollow tube is a long cylinder-shaped object, a solid with circular cross-section.

clue.text: On the first of the month, Charlie got infected

parts.note: Sept is the short form of September
I is the Roman numeral one, the first
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: On the first day of the month, someone called Charlie picked up an infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first of the month' reads as a date, Sept I, with the Roman one.
explanation.definitionFit: A wound that has turned septic is infected with bacteria.

clue.text: Storm over replica Twombly

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the artist's first name above the copy

parts.note: Cy Twombly was an American abstract painter
a clone is an exact copy

explanation.surface: A furore about a copy of a Cy Twombly painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storm' looks like a verb but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent rotating weather system is a type of storm.

clue.text: American cobblers' links traceable back to Emilia Romagna?

definitions.meaning: cobblers is British rhyming slang (cobblers' awls, balls) for nonsense; the American word for nonsense is meant

definitions.text: links traceable back to Emilia Romagna?
definitions.meaning: links are sausages; the US name for the Bologna sausage comes from the city of Bologna in Emilia-Romagna

explanation.surface: The links of American shoemakers seem to trace back to northern Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cobblers' looks like shoemakers but is British slang for rubbish; 'links' are a chain of sausages.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is US slang for nonsense and also the American spelling of Bologna sausage.

clue.text: British view gets slapped on the wrist!

definitions.note: read as a description of a thing put on the wrist, an ornament, rather than a reprimand

parts.note: an angle is a point of view

explanation.surface: A British opinion is reprimanded mildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slapped on the wrist' sounds like a mild telling-off but describes jewellery pushed on.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigid bracelet is pushed on to be worn around the wrist.

clue.text: Crush the spirit

definitions.meaning: to put an end to, as a rumour is quashed

explanation.surface: Stamp out the morale of the opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to stamp out a rumour or idea, and the noun is whisky distilled in Scotland.

clue.text: Smug, being able to have lake in Provence for most of summer there

indicators.note: for means one piece takes the place of the other in the word for able

parts.note: competent means able

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped from the French word for summer

parts.note: été is French for summer, the language of Provence
lac is French for lake

explanation.surface: Self-satisfied at being able to own a lake in Provence for most of the summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there' points to France: ÉTÉ trimmed by 'most of' to ET is replaced in COMPETENT by LAC, signalled by 'for'.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-satisfied and uncritically pleased with oneself is a synonym for smug.

clue.text: Lonely ol' mam working with Meals on Wheels?

definitions.note: a playful description of the Dublin fishmonger of the song, who wheeled her wheelbarrow of cockles and mussels

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A lonely old mum volunteers for the meals service delivering food to the elderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges LONELY OL MAM. Meals on Wheels is a British charity delivering hot food to housebound people.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of the Dublin ballad sold seafood from a barrow, so her food literally went about on wheels.

clue.text: Swapped sides of stupid boy's hat

indicators.note: the two halves of the name change places, front pair going to the back

parts.note: Private Pike in the British sitcom Dad's Army is called 'stupid boy' by Captain Mainwaring

explanation.surface: Someone has switched round the sides of a silly lad's cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swapped sides of' turns PI-KE into KE-PI. Dad's Army is a classic BBC comedy about the Home Guard.
explanation.definitionFit: A French military cap with a flat circular top and peak is a kind of hat.

clue.text: Shell tycoon upset for a few minutes

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read bottom to top
shell means the outside of the word is removed, as a nut is shelled

parts.note: a fat cat is a wealthy tycoon

explanation.surface: An oil-company magnate is distressed for a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shell' strips F and T from FAT CAT to leave ATCA, which 'upset' reverses. Shell looks like the oil firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Acta are official records of proceedings, the minutes of a meeting.

clue.text: They connected a line in motel corridor

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the words motel corridor

explanation.surface: Someone ran a phone line into a hotel hallway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the run of letters across MOTEL CORRIDOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone company is the firm that connects your phone line to the network.

clue.text: One ignorant of sibling behaviour merely told off detained student

parts.note: only means merely

indicators.note: detained means held inside, so the student is kept within the word for told off

parts.note: chid is an old past tense of chide, to scold
L is a learner, from the L-plate

explanation.surface: A student behaving badly is scolded and kept in after school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detained' puts L inside CHID, an archaic past of chide; 'behaviour' looks like the student's conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without brothers or sisters never experiences how siblings act toward each other.

clue.text: Play causing discomfort for the viewers?

definitions.meaning: an allergy that makes the eyes itch and stream; viewers here are eyes

explanation.surface: A theatre piece that makes the audience uncomfortable.
explanation.definitionFit: Coward's 1925 comedy shares its title with the pollen allergy that inflames the eyes.
